title: Schrijver-Delsarte rigidity in association schemes and undecidability of quantum graph homomorphism
authors: Lorenzo Ciardo, Iris Hebbeker, Gideo Joubert, Jana Kreiß, Antoine Mottet
abstract: We prove RE-completeness of the quantum homomorphism problem parameterised by families of graphs derived from the classic metric association schemes. These include Kneser graphs, $q$-Kneser graphs, and the complements of Johnson, Grassmann, and Hamming graphs. Our proof develops a spectral method for establishing non-contextuality of quantum polymorphisms. It combines an equality analysis of Roberson's bound on the projective packing number in terms of Schrijver's theta with a structural argument inspired by Erdős-Ko-Rado theory.
summary: This theoretical paper proves that determining if a quantum homomorphism exists for certain structured graphs (like Kneser graphs) is computationally hard (RE-complete). It achieves this by developing a novel spectral method that links graph rigidity properties (derived from association schemes) to the non-contextuality of quantum operations. The work significantly advances the understanding of complexity in quantum graph theory.
main_problem: The paper determines the computational complexity of the quantum graph homomorphism problem parameterized by specific families of graphs derived from association schemes.
main_result: It proves that this quantum homomorphism problem is RE-complete for graphs like Kneser graphs and complements of Johnson/Grassmann/Hamming graphs.
method: The proof develops a spectral method to establish the non-contextuality of quantum polymorphisms, combining analysis of Roberson's bound with structural arguments from EKR theory.
model_or_system: The model involves the quantum graph homomorphism problem defined over finite-dimensional tensor-product oracular settings, utilizing concepts from algebraic combinatorics like association schemes.
key_observables: Quantum homomorphism problem, Projective Packing Number (alpha_p(G)), Schrijver's theta (vartheta^-), and quantum polymorphisms.
important_parameters: The graph structure derived from symmetric association schemes (e.g., Kneser, Hamming).
main_assumptions: The method relies on establishing a spectral condition that forces quantum polymorphisms to be non-contextual, linking graph rigidity to computational complexity.

paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the quantum homomorphism problem and related bounds ($\alpha_p, \vartheta^-$) to developing a spectral criterion for non-contextuality. It then applies this criterion to specific graph families (like those from association schemes) to prove RE-completeness.
why_interesting: While highly mathematical, establishing computational hardness results for quantum problems provides theoretical boundaries for quantum computation models, which is relevant to understanding the limits of quantum information processing.

figures.caption: Figure 1: The Kneser graph KG(7, 3). Its vertex labels are the 3-subsets of [7] = {1, . . . , 7}, and two vertices are adjacent precisely when the corresponding subsets are disjoint. The graph has 35 vertices and 70 edges.

Figure 2: The complement J(7, 3) of the Johnson graph. Its vertex labels are the 3-subsets of [7] = {1, . . . , 7}, and two distinct vertices x, y are adjacent precisely when |x ∩y| ≤1. The graph has 35 vertices and 385 edges.

Figure 3: The graph KG2(4, 2) = J2(4, 2), which is both a q-Kneser graph and the complement of a Grassmann graph. Its 35 vertices are the two-dimensional subspaces of F4 2. We identify each integer r ∈{0, . . . , 15} with its four-bit binary representation in F4 2; each vertex label lists the four elements of the corresponding subspace. Two vertices are adjacent precisely when the corresponding subspaces intersect only in 0. The graph has 280 edges.

Figure 4: The complement H(3, 3) of the Hamming graph H(3, 3). The label x1x2x3 denotes the word (x1, x2, x3) ∈{1, 2, 3}3, and two distinct words are adjacent precisely when their Hamming distance is at least 2. The graph has 27 vertices and 270 edges.
